title: Dataverse security roles: who can read or change which data?
summary: Hold: the privileges automation creates a role but does not grant its privileges, and Microsoft documents automation for two controls described as undocumented. The page also overstates the Environment Maker requirement for agent authors and gives unconditional advice to copy roles that Microsoft says cannot always be copied.

claims.where: controls[0].ui
claims.claim: The environment's security-role privileges are reached through Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + Permissions > Security roles.
claims.quote: Select Manage in the navigation pane. ... Select Users + Permissions > Security roles.
claims.fix: Append '> security role' to the path to identify the role being configured. The editing procedure at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/create-edit-security-role says to choose the security role and then specify its privileges.

claims.where: controls[0].api
claims.claim: POST [Organization Uri]/api/data/v9.2/roles sets which privileges and access levels a role grants.
claims.quote: 1. Create a security role. You must associate the role with a business unit. ... 6. Pass the list as the AddPrivilegesRole.Privileges parameter.
claims.fix: Replace the call with 'POST [Organization Uri]/api/data/v9.2/roles(<role-id>)/Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.AddPrivilegesRole', keeping the existing sample URL as docs. Replace the creation-body sentence in the note with 'The Privileges request-body array supplies RolePrivilege entries, including PrivilegeId and Depth.' This is the sample's operation that adds privileges.

claims.where: controls[1].ui
claims.claim: User role assignments are managed at Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Users > user > Manage security roles.
claims.quote: Select Users + permissions, and then select Users. ... On the Users page select a user, and then select Manage security roles.

claims.where: controls[1].api
claims.claim: The printed v9.0 systemuserroles_association POST assigns a role to a user, with the role reference in @odata.id.
claims.quote: POST [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.0/systemusers(azureactivedirectoryobjectid=<user object ID>)/systemuserroles_association/$ref

claims.where: controls[2].ui
claims.claim: Application-user role configuration is reached through Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Application users > + New app user.
claims.quote: Select + New app user to open the Create a new app user pane. ... Select the edit icon to select security roles for the new application user.
claims.fix: The printed steps are correct but stop before the unlabelled role-edit icon. Append this to the note: 'In Create a new app user, choose the application and business unit, then select the edit icon to select security roles.'

claims.where: controls[2].api
claims.claim: pac admin assign-user accepts the printed environment, application ID, role and application-user switch to assign an application user's role.
claims.quote: Assign a user to a target Dataverse environment with specified security role. ... Application ID if assigning an Application User. ... Specifies whether the input user is an application user.

claims.where: controls[3].ui
claims.claim: License-to-role mapping can be viewed at Environments > environment > Settings > Users + Permissions > License To Role mapping.
claims.quote: Go to Environments > [select an environment] > Settings > Users + Permissions > License To Role mapping.

claims.where: controls[3].api; Open questions
claims.claim: An API or command for License To Role mapping was not found.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Dataverse License To Role mapping API licensetypemapping table PowerShell' and '"License To Role mapping" "API"'; read assign-security-roles and pac admin. Results documented the UI, not a mapping operation.

claims.where: controls[4].ui
claims.claim: Record ownership across business units is at Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features.
claims.quote: Select Settings > Product > Features. ... Turn on Record ownership across business units.

claims.where: controls[4].api; Open questions
claims.claim: No API or command is documented for Record ownership across business units.
claims.quote: To update Microsoft.Crm.SE.OrgDBOrgSettingsTool.exe Update [/u] <OrgName> <SettingName> <Value>
claims.fix: Set this API side to kind 'other', call 'Microsoft.Crm.SE.OrgDBOrgSettingsTool.exe Update /u <organization-unique-name> EnableOwnershipAcrossBusinessUnits true', and docs to the source URL. The already-cited ownership-security page explicitly identifies this setting and this tool. Remove Record ownership across business units from the Open questions claim that neither command was found.

claims.where: controls[5].ui
claims.claim: The printed audit-settings path reaches Security Role > General > Auditing.
claims.quote: In the left side panel, under Entities, select Security Role. ... On the General tab, under Data Services, select Auditing.
claims.fix: Use 'Environments > environment > Settings > Audit and logs > Entity and field audit settings > Entities > Security Role > General > Data Services > Auditing'. Entities and Data Services are omitted headings, not missing selectable choices.

claims.where: controls[5].api
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented automation for enabling the security-role audit trail.
claims.quote: To change which tables and columns support auditing, update their IsAuditEnabled.Value property.
claims.fix: Replace the null side with kind 'rest', call "PUT [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/EntityDefinitions(LogicalName='role')", docs 'https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/create-update-entity-definitions-using-web-api'. Add to the note: 'Set IsAuditEnabled.Value in the retrieved table definition, preserving the other definition properties; publish the table customizations for the change to take effect.' Cite the configure-auditing source as well.

claims.where: summary; What it is
claims.claim: Dataverse security roles group the privileges governing users', teams' and application users' access to tables and records in an environment.
claims.quote: Dataverse uses security roles to group privileges. Assign security roles directly to users or to Dataverse teams. Team members receive the privileges assigned to the team.

claims.where: What it is
claims.claim: The Dataverse security model applies to environments with a Dataverse database.
claims.quote: The model applies only to environments that have a Dataverse database.

claims.where: What it is: How a role is built
claims.claim: Roles contain table, miscellaneous task and privacy-related privileges.
claims.quote: A security role consists of record-level privileges and task-based privileges of the following three types: ... Tables ... Miscellaneous privileges ... Privacy-related privileges

claims.where: What it is: How a role is built
claims.claim: Table privileges include Create, Read, Write, Delete, Append, Append To, Assign and Share.
claims.quote: Table privileges define which tasks a user with access to a table record can do, such as Read, Create, Delete, Write, Assign, Share, Append, and Append To.

claims.where: What it is: How a role is built
claims.claim: Privacy-related privileges include exporting data to Excel.
claims.quote: These privileges give a user permission to perform tasks that involve data that's integrated, downloaded, or exported outside of Dataverse, such as exporting data to Microsoft Excel or printing.

claims.where: What it is: How a role is built
claims.claim: Privilege access levels determine business-unit reach and are Organization, Parent: Child Business Unit, Business Unit, User or None.
claims.quote: Access levels determine how deep in the business unit hierarchy the user can perform the privilege.

claims.where: What it is: How a role reaches a person
claims.claim: Users receive privileges from roles assigned directly or through Dataverse teams.
claims.quote: A user's effective access combines directly assigned security roles with roles assigned through teams. Dataverse always grants the broadest permission from those roles.

claims.where: What it is: How a role reaches a person; Why it matters; Risks and limits
claims.claim: Multiple roles are cumulative, and a narrower role cannot remove access another role or team grants.
claims.quote: Security privileges are cumulative. A user receives the broadest access granted by all their roles and team memberships. ... another role can't hide a specific contact from the user.

claims.where: What it is: How a role reaches a person
claims.claim: Business units define security boundaries.
claims.quote: Business units work with security roles to determine a user's access. They define security boundaries that help you manage users and data.

claims.where: What it is: How a role reaches a person
claims.claim: Every user belongs to a business unit.
claims.quote: Every user in an environment belongs to a business unit.

claims.where: What it is; Governance controls: How the controls interact
claims.claim: Roles belong to business units, and enabling record ownership across business units permits assignments from other business units.
claims.quote: When the allow record ownership across business units is enabled, you can assign security roles from different business units to your users irrespective of which business unit the users belong to.

claims.where: What it is: Roles that are not Dataverse roles
claims.claim: Tenant-level roles such as Power Platform administrator are assigned in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Tenant-level admin roles such as Power Platform administrator and Dynamics 365 administrator are assigned in the Microsoft 365 admin center and grant administrative access across environments.

claims.where: What it is: Roles that are not Dataverse roles; Risks and limits
claims.claim: A tenant admin's role alone does not grant Dataverse data access; Microsoft specifies System Administrator in that environment.
claims.quote: To work with data in a Dataverse environment, a tenant admin must also be assigned the System Administrator Dataverse security role in that specific environment.

claims.where: What it is: Roles that are not Dataverse roles
claims.claim: Environments without a Dataverse database use Environment Admin and Environment Maker as their predefined environment roles.
claims.quote: Environment Maker and Environment Admin are the only predefined roles for environments that have no Dataverse database.

claims.where: What it is; Risks and limits: Sharing is the exception
claims.claim: Microsoft advises record sharing for exceptions because it is less efficient and harder to troubleshoot.
claims.quote: Use sharing only for exceptions because it performs less efficiently and can be harder to troubleshoot than role-based access.

claims.where: What it is; Risks and limits: Roles do not unlock columns
claims.claim: Column-level security is configured separately and requires record access before a column security profile grants secured-column access.
claims.quote: Enable column-level security separately for each column. ... A user must already have record access before a column security profile can grant access to secured columns.

claims.where: What it is; Risks and limits: Filtered record ownership
claims.claim: Filtered record ownership is preview and grants record access through column-value filters.
claims.quote: Filtered table record ownership (preview) ... Filtered record ownership lets admins control access to Dataverse records with column-value filters.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Filtered record ownership
claims.claim: Microsoft says preview features are not meant for production use.
claims.quote: Preview features aren't meant for production use and may have restricted functionality.

claims.where: Why it matters; What to check
claims.claim: Basic User and Environment Maker are automatically assigned to all users added to Dataverse in the Default environment type.
claims.quote: For the Default environment type, Basic User and Environment Maker roles are assigned automatically to all users added in Dataverse.

claims.where: Why it matters
claims.claim: Copilot Studio authoring depends on Environment Maker.
claims.quote: Assign the Environment Maker role to users who need to author agents. If the user needs a different set of permissions, assign another predefined role or a custom role.
claims.fix: Replace 'Copilot Studio authoring depends on Environment Maker' with 'Microsoft recommends Environment Maker for Copilot Studio authors, or another predefined or custom role with the needed permissions'. The same page lists System Administrator and System Customizer as other authoring roles.

claims.where: Why it matters
claims.claim: Tenant administrators are no longer automatically assigned Dataverse System Administrator.
claims.quote: Power Platform, Dynamics 365, and Global Administrators are no longer automatically assigned the Dataverse System Administrator role.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: Tenant admin is not data access
claims.claim: Removing a tenant admin role does not automatically remove an earlier Dataverse System Administrator assignment.
claims.quote: removing them from the Power Platform admin and Dynamics 365 service admin roles will not automatically remove their System Administrator role in Dataverse.

claims.where: Why it matters
claims.claim: Neither automatic assignment state is visible without examining assignments in each environment.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse security roles privileges assign application users ownership based security audit security roles; read security-roles-privileges, assign-security-roles and audit-security-roles. They document inspection routes, not an exclusive visibility limitation.
claims.fix: Replace 'Neither state is visible without looking at the role assignments in each environment' with the advice 'Review the role assignments in each environment'.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Microsoft's role documentation does not publish a separate role-specific price, licence or meter.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Dataverse security roles separate price license meter'; read security-roles-privileges, database-security, wp-security-cds and pricing-billing-skus. These discuss product access licensing, not a separate charge for security roles.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Presence in an environment does not grant Dataverse data access; an appropriate role and any required product licence are still needed.
claims.quote: A user's presence in an environment doesn't grant access to Dataverse data. The user must still have an appropriate security role and any required product license.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Dataverse tracks access per database and requires an appropriate Dataverse licence.
claims.quote: Dataverse tracks access separately for each database, and the user must have an appropriate Dataverse license.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Where licence-to-role mappings exist, valid licences result in automatic assignment of mapped roles.
claims.quote: Users, with a valid license, get corresponding mapped roles assigned to them automatically.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Removing the corresponding licence automatically removes the mapped role.
claims.quote: Removal of the respective license results in automatic role removal.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; controls[3].note
claims.claim: Licence-based default role management does not apply to Dataverse for Teams, Trial or Developer environments.
claims.quote: License-based default role management isn't applicable for users in these types of environments: Dataverse for Teams, Trial, and Developer.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: An application user can be created without a licence.
claims.quote: You can create an unlicensed application user in your environment.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Dataverse audit logs consume log storage capacity.
claims.quote: Dataverse stores audit logs and they consume log storage capacity.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Everyone needs a role
claims.claim: Users need at least one security role, directly or through a group team, for service access.
claims.quote: You must assign at least one security role to every user either directly or indirectly as a member of a group team. The service doesn't allow access to users who don't have at least one security role.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Elevation guard
claims.claim: A role assigner cannot assign another person a role with more privileges than the assigner holds.
claims.quote: the person who is assigning the security role can't assign someone else to a security role that has more privileges than the assigner.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Elevation guard
claims.claim: Delegating role assignment to non-System Administrators uses a custom Dataverse role with the required privileges.
claims.quote: Assign Dataverse security roles | System Administrator security role, or a custom Dataverse role with at least Read and Assign privileges on the Security Role table

claims.where: Risks and limits: Predefined roles cannot be edited; controls[0].note
claims.claim: Predefined security roles cannot be edited.
claims.quote: The following list provides the predefined security roles in an environment that has a Dataverse database. You can't edit these roles.
claims.fix: Attribute the restriction to the predefined-role reference and acknowledge that https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/create-edit-security-role documents editing role privileges while specifically excluding System Administrator. Replace the blanket wording with 'The predefined-role reference says its listed roles cannot be edited; Microsoft's editing guide separately documents editing role privileges, except System Administrator.'

claims.where: Risks and limits: Predefined roles cannot be edited
claims.claim: Copy a predefined role whenever it needs changing.
claims.quote: Some predefined roles can't be copied. Try creating a custom security role instead.
claims.fix: Replace 'Copy a role to change it' with 'Where copying is supported, copy the role and change the copy; some predefined roles cannot be copied, so create a custom role instead'.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Predefined roles cannot be edited
claims.claim: Custom security roles are not supported for canvas apps.
claims.quote: It's important to note that custom security roles are not supported for canvas apps.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Organization-level access; What to check
claims.claim: Organization-level access reaches records across all business units.
claims.quote: Users can access all records in the organization, regardless of the business unit hierarchical level they or the environment belong to.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Moving between environments
claims.claim: Dataverse solutions can move security roles between environments.
claims.quote: Use Dataverse solutions to move security roles and column security profiles between environments.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Moving between environments
claims.claim: Business units, teams and user security assignments are managed separately in each environment.
claims.quote: Create and manage business units and teams separately in each environment. You must also assign users to the appropriate security components in each environment.

claims.where: Risks and limits: PowerShell gap; Open questions
claims.claim: Set-AdminPowerAppEnvironmentRoleAssignment applies to environments without Dataverse and returns 403 for environments with a Dataverse database.
claims.quote: Sets permissions to an environment without a Dataverse database. If you make this call to an environment with a Dataverse database instance, you receive a 403 Forbidden error.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls: Who can change roles
claims.claim: Assigning roles requires System Administrator or a custom role with at least Read and Assign on the Security Role table.
claims.quote: Assign Dataverse security roles | System Administrator security role, or a custom Dataverse role with at least Read and Assign privileges on the Security Role table
claims.fix: Keep the precise prerequisite, but add: 'The general role overview's troubleshooting table instead says only System Administrator or a tenant-level admin can manage assignments; the task-specific assignment and access-control documentation explicitly permits the qualified custom role.' The differing page is https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/database-security#common-issues.

claims.where: Governance controls: Who can change roles; What to check
claims.claim: Power Platform, Dynamics 365 and Global Administrators must self-elevate before assigning Dataverse roles.
claims.quote: Power Platform, Dynamics 365, and Global Administrators are no longer automatically assigned the Dataverse System Administrator role. They must self-elevate before assigning Dataverse roles.

claims.where: Governance controls: Who can change roles
claims.claim: A Dynamics 365 Administrator must belong to the environment's security group.
claims.quote: A Dynamics 365 Administrator must belong to the environment's security group. This restriction doesn't apply to Global Administrators or Power Platform Administrators.

claims.where: controls[4].note
claims.claim: The documented UI procedure for record ownership across business units requires a Dynamics 365 admin or Power Platform admin.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Power Platform admin center as a Dynamics 365 admin or Microsoft Power Platform admin.

claims.where: controls[4].note
claims.claim: Microsoft names OrgDBOrgSettings as a tool for changing the underlying cross-business-unit ownership setting.
claims.quote: The EnableOwnershipAcrossBusinessUnits setting stores the state of this feature. You can also change the setting with the OrgDBOrgSettings tool for Microsoft Dynamics CRM.

claims.where: controls[0].note
claims.claim: The role-creation request body sets name and businessunitid@odata.bind.
claims.quote:
"businessunitid@odata.bind": "businessunits(cca3985e-c618-ea11-a811-000d3a33f066)",
"name": "Test Role"

claims.where: controls[0].note
claims.claim: AddPrivilegesRole adds privileges to an existing role.
claims.quote: Adds a set of existing privileges to an existing role.

claims.where: controls[2].note
claims.claim: An environment can have only one application user per Microsoft Entra app registration.
claims.quote: In an environment, you can only have one application user for each Microsoft Entra–registered application.

claims.where: controls[5].note; Governance controls: How the controls interact
claims.claim: Security-role auditing requires auditing to be enabled in the environment first.
claims.quote: Prerequisites ... Turn on auditing in your environment.

claims.where: controls[5].note; What to check
claims.claim: The security-role audit report is reached from the environment's Settings > Users + permissions > Security roles > Audit report.
claims.quote: Select Environments > [select an environment] > Settings > Users + permissions > Security roles. ... Select Audit report in the command bar.

claims.where: Governance controls: How the controls interact
claims.claim: Audit event 53 records assigning a role to a team.
claims.quote: 53 | Assign Role To Team | Associate | A security role is assigned to a team.

claims.where: Governance controls: How the controls interact
claims.claim: Audit event 54 records removing a role from a team.
claims.quote: 54 | Remove Role From Team | Disassociate | A security role is removed from a team.

claims.where: Governance controls: How the controls interact
claims.claim: Audit event 55 records assigning a role to a user.
claims.quote: 55 | Assign Role To User | Associate | A security role is assigned to a user.

claims.where: Governance controls: How the controls interact
claims.claim: Audit event 56 records removing a role from a user.
claims.quote: 56 | Remove Role From User | Disassociate | A security role is removed from a user.

claims.where: Governance controls: How the controls interact
claims.claim: Licence-to-role mapping adds roles on top of manual assignments.
claims.quote: Searched: '"license" "manually assigned" "roles" Dataverse' and '"security role" "assignments" "license" "manual" Dataverse'; read assign-security-roles. It documents automatic assignment/removal, not preservation or interaction with manual assignments.
claims.fix: Replace the sentence with 'Where licence-to-role mapping is defined, roles are assigned automatically according to the user's licence'.

claims.where: Governance controls: What the controls do not enforce
claims.claim: Security roles do not govern which connectors a flow uses.
claims.quote: Searched: '"security roles" "connectors" "data policies" "flows"' and 'Dataverse "security roles" "don't" "connectors"'; read role documentation and Data policies excerpts. Data policies govern connectors, but no passage establishes the blanket exclusion.
claims.fix: Replace this clause with 'Data policies let administrators control connector access (see Data policies)' and cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/wp-data-loss-prevention. Do not claim that roles cannot affect connector use.

claims.where: Governance controls: What the controls do not enforce
claims.claim: Security roles do not set environment-level limits.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Managed Environments" "limits" "security roles"'; read managed-environment-overview and database-security. They describe separate capabilities but do not state that no security-role privilege governs any environment-level limit.
claims.fix: Remove 'do not set environment-level limits'. The Managed Environments cross-link may remain as a cross-link without this universal exclusion.

claims.where: Governance controls: What the controls do not enforce
claims.claim: Security roles do not decide whose identity an agent runs as.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot Studio agent identity Dataverse security roles agent application user runtime' and 'Dataverse security roles "authentication" "authorization"'; read govern-agents-identities-overview. Automatic identity provisioning does not establish this universal runtime claim.
claims.fix: Remove 'do not decide whose identity an agent runs as'. Retain the Agent identity cross-link without the unsupported exclusion.

claims.where: Open questions: PowerShell
claims.claim: A Power Platform administration PowerShell cmdlet for assigning Dataverse security roles was not found.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Dataverse assign security role PowerShell Microsoft.PowerApps.Administration Add role'; read Set-AdminPowerAppEnvironmentRoleAssignment and assignment documentation. The administration cmdlet found explicitly excludes Dataverse databases.

claims.where: Open questions: filtered record ownership
claims.claim: A general-availability date or a feature-specific licence or add-on for filtered record ownership was not found.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Dataverse filtered record ownership preview licensing general availability'; read filtered-view-record-ownership, wp-security-cds and pricing-billing-skus. Preview is stated, but no GA date or filter-specific licence/add-on is given.

claims.where: Open questions: agents themselves
claims.claim: How role-based privileges apply to agents themselves, rather than their makers, is not documented.
claims.quote: Dataverse enforces table privileges, field-level security, ownership and sharing, and administrator permissions on every request. An agent can't exceed the permissions of the signed-in identity.
claims.fix: Remove this open question. The absence is too broad: Microsoft documents runtime enforcement for the Dataverse plugin for AI agents in preview. The qualification 'on the pages read' does not establish a general documentation gap.

claims.where: sources
claims.claim: The role-editing route is supported by a Microsoft page not listed in sources.
claims.quote: Choose the security role you want to edit. ... Specify privileges for the security role.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/create-edit-security-role to sources. For the corrections above, also cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/wp-data-loss-prevention, https://support.microsoft.com/help/2691237/orgdborgsettings-tool-for-microsoft-dynamics-crm, https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/auditing/configure and https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/create-update-entity-definitions-using-web-api where their facts are retained.
